hmmt-feb-2008-gen2-01.title: Complementary counting
hmmt-feb-2008-gen2-01.body:
There are $\binom95=126$ ways to choose $5$ of the $9$ students. Bad choices: all five from MIT ($1$ way), or neither Jack nor Jill goes, i.e. all $5$ come from the other $7$ ($\binom75=21$ ways). These two bad cases do not overlap (the MIT group contains Jill). So the count is $126-1-21=104$.

**Answer: 104**

hmmt-feb-2008-gen2-04.title: Lagrange identity
hmmt-feb-2008-gen2-04.body:
$(ab-cd)^2+(ac+bd)^2=(a^2+d^2)(b^2+c^2)=1$ (expand: both sides equal $a^2b^2+a^2c^2+d^2b^2+d^2c^2$). So $(ab-cd)^2=1-\frac19=\frac89$. Since $a\ge c$ and $b\ge d$ with all numbers non-negative, $ab\ge cd$, so $ab-cd=\frac{2\sqrt2}3$.

**Answer: $\frac{2\sqrt2}3$**

hmmt-feb-2008-gen2-04.title: Trigonometric substitution
hmmt-feb-2008-gen2-04.body:
Write $a=\sin\theta$, $d=\cos\theta$, $b=\sin\varphi$, $c=\cos\varphi$ with angles in $[0,\frac\pi2]$. Then $ac+bd=\sin(\theta+\varphi)=\frac13$ and $ab-cd=-\cos(\theta+\varphi)$, which is non-negative here, so $ab-cd=\sqrt{1-\frac19}=\frac{2\sqrt2}3$.

**Answer: $\frac{2\sqrt2}3$**
